pages.text: Cepheid variables pulse with a period that gives their true brightness: the first rung of the distance ladder. A Spectrograph sets a $(item)Cepheid Standard Candle$() against a spectral plate: a $(item)Redshift Lens$() - every galaxy is receding, faster the farther.

A long survey of the hydrogen line maps a $(item)Galactic Filament$(). Four of them and a Redshift Lens, run through the Monte Carlo Engine, trace the $(item)Cosmic Web$(): the filaments and voids gravity has drawn the dark matter into since the Big Bang.
For the Universe to be flat, it must hold the $(thing)critical density$() ρ = 3H²/8πG - about five protons in every cubic metre.
